- **claim-off-gap-path-contradiction** (theorem, [source](#stmt-act-off-gap-path)): Suppose that on an open time interval and in a sufficiently narrow right neighborhood of $v=Jt$ the following hold. The profiles $E,E^g$ are nonnegative and uniformly Lipschitz on the compact domains used, satisfy <a href="#eq:enl" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:enl">[eq:enl]</a>, and $E_t(Jt)=0$. Equations <a href="#eq:step" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:step">[eq:step]</a> and <a href="#eq:shift" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:shift">[eq:shift]</a> apply, with bounded step speeds whose minimum is at least $1$ and strictly greater than $J$; step admissibility is uniform on compact subsets for $h/g$ small enough. The angular rate has its nondecreasing-in-$t$ version. There is a speed $k_+\ge1$, $k_+>J$, for which <a href="#eq:surplus" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:surplus">[eq:surplus]</a> holds almost everywhere where $m_t(v)>0$. Alternatively, that motion need only hold for $0<m_t(v)\le k_0$ provided the vertical estimate $\partial_tE_t(v)\le-2\Gamma$ holds almost everywhere where $m_t(v)>k_0$, throughout the constant-width continuations used, including after crossing the seam. The normal-width exponent has positive forward rate on all branches needed for <a href="#eq:shift" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:shift">[eq:shift]</a>. These conditions are incompatible with $\Gamma>0$.
  - Explanation: Finite steps through zero-trace regions and differential motion through positive-trace regions contradict nonnegativity and seam equality when the exponent is positive.
- **claim-round-packet-locality** (bound, [source](#stmt-rt-packet-locality)): For $\ell'\le\ell$ and $\|u\|\lesssim\ell$, the kernel of $V_{\ell'}U(u)V_\ell^*$ vanishes unless $\|A'-A\|\lesssim d_{\ell'}$. On this angular support its absolute value is at most $$\frac{C_N}{q_\ell^2H} \left(1+\frac{\|b'-b-uA\|}{q_\ell} +\frac{\|y'-y-u\|A\|^2-2A\cdot(b'-b-uA)\|}{H}\right)^{-N}. \tag{cone-kernel}\label{eq:cone-kernel}$$ Consequently, after any fixed finite stack, retained correspondence paths from a row at cut $i$ to a row at cut $j$ satisfy $$\begin{split} \|A_j-A\|&\le s^{-O(\varepsilon)}d_{\ell_j},\\ \|b_j-b^p\|&\le s^{-O(\varepsilon)}q_{\ell_i},\\ \|y_j-y^p-2A\cdot(b_j-b^p)\|&\le s^{-O(\varepsilon)}H. \end{split} \tag{acc}\label{eq:acc}$$ Here $(b^p,y^p)$ is the prediction along the earlier row’s ray. Removing all kernel pairs outside these correspondences changes the operators by an arbitrarily small power error, for every prescribed $\varepsilon>0$.
  - Explanation: Compact angular support and rapidly decaying spatial kernels control finite-stack packet correspondences and negligible nonconnections.
- **claim-round-enlarged-tests** (bound, [source](#stmt-rt-covering)): Suppose $P\ge2$. Enlarge the normalized round bounds by fixed powers of $P$, allow coefficients bounded by fixed powers of $P$ with discriminant one, and replace both sublevels by $P^Cf$. The resulting set has mass at most $\kappa r^4f^{1-\eta}P^{C'}$, provided $rf\ge d_\ell$. The exponent $C'$ depends only on the stated enlargement exponents. Restriction, synthesis, and plateau reanalysis at one cut consequently preserve regularity with an arbitrarily small exponent loss.
  - Explanation: Polynomial enlargements of normalized round tests have controlled regularity cost, allowing restriction, synthesis and plateau reanalysis.
- **claim-round-single-time-bound** (bound, [source](#stmt-rt-single)): Relative to regularity at a parent cut, the energy in a test of widths $(r,f)$ at any one descendant of relative length $\delta$ satisfies $$m\le s^{-o(1)}\kappa r^4 f^{1-\eta}\delta. \tag{single}\label{eq:single}$$ The same conclusion holds through any fixed finite stack.
  - Explanation: Round regularity at a parent bounds a descendant test mass with the relative duration factor, including a fixed finite operator stack.
- **claim-free-gap-composition** (bound, [source](#stmt-rt-free-composition)): Inserting finitely many admissible pointwise row contractions followed by synthesis, as in Definition <a href="#rt:model" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="rt:model">90</a>, at fixed depths does not increase $\Gamma$. Repeated operations at the same cut are permitted. Reconstruction uses plateau analyses, while an old non-plateau terminal analysis may be retained for coherent recombination.
  - Explanation: Finite row contractions and synthesis do not increase the free round growth exponent when the stated analysis conventions are preserved.
- **claim-round-inserted-cut-saturation** (classification, [source](#stmt-rt-saturation)): Suppose $\Gamma>0$. In the outer closure of homogeneous free exponent data, let $p_0$ be the minimal mass exponent at upper exponent $\Gamma$, and let $d$ be the associated total-mass exponent. Then $$\Gamma=d+(1-p_0)/2,\qquad p_0\ge1,\qquad 0<d\le1.$$ Fix any finite depth list. After realizing these data with arbitrarily small exterior errors, every regularity splitting preserving the terminal functional has limiting dominant regularity and summed energy described by $$\kappa_a=\kappa s^{p_0a+o(1)},\qquad E_a=e s^{-da+o(1)}. \tag{CE}\label{eq:CE}$$ In particular, an arbitrarily short fixed final gap may be taken free, with a regularly split incoming state, when classifying terminal shapes. Equation <a href="#eq:CE" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:CE">[eq:CE]</a> denotes identities of exponent data in this outer closure; it does not assert that one inner sequence attains the closure extrema exactly.
  - Explanation: Minimal homogeneous free data force energy and regularity saturation at preserving inserted cuts in the outer closure, without asserting exact inner attainment.
- **claim-thin-round-cylinder-reduction** (bound, [source](#stmt-rt-thin-exclusion)): Let $\Gamma_{\rm cl}^{\rm cyl}$ and $\Gamma_{\rm hyb}^{\rm cyl}$ be the classical and hybrid cylinder exponents. A saturated round experiment with terminal thickness of positive limiting exponent satisfies $$\Gamma\le\Gamma_{\rm cl}^{\rm cyl} \quad\hbox{in the classical case},\qquad \Gamma\le\max(\Gamma_{\rm cl}^{\rm cyl},\Gamma_{\rm hyb}^{\rm cyl}) \quad\hbox{in the wave case}.$$ The conclusion includes infinite limiting thickness exponents.
  - Explanation: Saturated round endings with positive thickness exponent reduce to the relevant cylinder exponents, including infinite limiting thickness exponents.
- **claim-null-hyperquadric-chart** (construction, [source](#stmt-rt-conformal-chart)): Let $\|n\|\le P$, $P\ge2$, with discriminant one. Near any bounded ray on which $\|F(0)\|+\|L_AF\|$ is smaller than a sufficiently high inverse power of $P$, there is a rational conformal chart carrying $F=0$ to $b'_2=0$. A polynomial number of such charts cover the relevant rays. On buffered subcharts, both chart directions have derivative bounds $C_jP^{Cj+C}$, time along a ray increases at a rate comparable to one, and parabolic phase boxes of width $R\le1$ map into polynomial enlargements of boxes of the same width. The induced linear map on hyperquadric coefficients preserves the discriminant and has norm and inverse norm bounded by powers of $P$.
  - Explanation: Buffered rational conformal charts flatten null hyperquadrics with controlled derivatives, parabolic boxes and coefficient transformations.
- **claim-thin-predecessor-overlap** (bound, [source](#stmt-rt-thin-overlap)): For $K=\max(1,\min_\pm\|n_\lambda\pm n_{\lambda'}\|/f)$, $$\mu_0(S_\lambda\cap S_{\lambda'}) \le\kappa\delta^{-C-o(1)}f^{1-\eta}/K. \tag{CI}\label{eq:CI}$$ The fixed exponent $C$ is independent of $Z$ in Equation <a href="#rt:very-thin" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="rt:very-thin">[rt:very-thin]</a>.
  - Explanation: The overlap of thin predecessor sets decreases with the normalized coefficient distance, with a fixed gap loss independent of the thinness precision.
- **claim-conformal-wave-transport** (construction, [source](#stmt-rt-wave-transport)): Let $u$ be the free cone wave synthesized from the retained patch. There is an exact free cone wave $u'$ in the transformed variables, with a fixed positive radial band. At packet length $\ell=1$ or $\delta$, write $p\sim_\ell p'$ when the old row $p$ and transformed row $p'$ are close to the mapped and backflowed ray in angle, transverse position, and tilt-corrected vertical position, with respective widths $\delta^{-\gamma}d_\ell$, $\delta^{-\gamma}q_\ell$, and $\delta^{-\gamma}H$; for terminal rows, include the corresponding chart event time rounded to the $\delta$-lattice. Put $N_\ell(E')=\{p:p\sim_\ell p'\text{ for some }p'\in E'\}$. Let $\mu_{\rm in}$ be the retained raw old row-energy measure at the parent input, and let $\mu'_{\rm in}$ be the transformed analyzed row-energy measure at time $-1$. For every prescribed $\gamma>0$ and $N>0$, if $b$ and the auxiliary localization losses are sufficiently small and $Z$ sufficiently large, the following hold:* 1. *for every Borel set $E'$ of transformed input rows, $$\mu'_{\rm in}(E')\le \delta^{-\gamma}\mu_{\rm in}(N_1(E'))+C_N\delta^N e_L;$$* 2. *for any finite old terminal fractional assignments of masses $m_\lambda$, there are fractional assignments to $u'$ at the rounded times, each supported on rows associated with its old label, whose fractions sum to at most one on every transformed row. If $m'_\lambda$ is the mass aggregated over the rounded times for label $\lambda$, then $$m_\lambda\le\delta^{-\gamma}m'_\lambda+\epsilon_\lambda, \qquad \sum_\lambda\epsilon_\lambda\le C_N\delta^N e_L.$$* *The predecessor sets are measured in the completion of $\mu_{\rm in}$.
  - Explanation: An exact transformed free cone wave permits input-energy and terminal fractional-assignment comparisons through localized packet association.
- **claim-cell-capacity-allocation** (construction, [source](#stmt-rt-capacity)): Let $x_i$ and $y_j$ be energies in two finite measurable cell partitions, and let $A,D\ge1$ and $\epsilon_i\ge0$. Suppose $$x_i\le A\sum_{j\in\mathcal N(i)}y_j+\epsilon_i,$$ and every source cell $j$ belongs to at most $D$ sets $\mathcal N(i)$. Assignments $m_{\lambda i}$ with $\sum_\lambda m_{\lambda i}\le x_i$ can, after removing total mass at most $\sum_i\epsilon_i$, be transferred to the $y$-cells with every retained label losing at most a factor $AD$. Contributions from different cells may be aggregated back into the same label without an additional factor.
  - Explanation: Proportional allocation transfers label masses through bounded-overlap cell capacities after removing only the allowed additive errors.
- **claim-flattened-test-weight-comparison** (bound, [source](#stmt-rt-weight-comparison)): Fix a finite precision $L_0$. Consider ideal input cylinder tests with base and normal widths $R,F_0\in[\delta^{L_0},1]$, and shear coefficients bounded by $\delta^{-L_0}$. Suppose $f_*F_0\gtrsim d_1$. Their associated old input rows have mass at most $$\delta^{-C\gamma}\kappa f_*^{1-\eta}R^{3+\eta}F_0^{1-\eta}. \tag{lift}\label{eq:lift}$$ At output, split each connected old assignment by chart and rounded time. Each resulting assignment fits an ideal cylinder test of weight at most $$\delta^{-C\gamma}(f/f_*)^{1-\eta}. \tag{endlift}\label{eq:endlift}$$ The assertions remain true under sufficiently small fixed-power base errors and normal errors of size $\delta^{-C\gamma}\max(\delta^S,d_\ell/f_*)$ in velocity and $\ell$ times this in position, where $\ell=1$ or $\delta$ and $S$ is sufficiently large. The constants are independent of $Z$ once $Z$ is sufficiently large relative to these fixed precisions.
  - Explanation: Moderate cylinder tests control transformed input masses and terminal test weights, with specified comparison errors and uncertainty floors.
- **claim-classicalized-base-hybrid-state** (construction, [source](#stmt-rt-classical-base)): In the range Equation <a href="#rt:normal-quantum-range" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="rt:normal-quantum-range">[rt:normal-quantum-range]</a>, the transformed wave can be replaced, for the input and terminal comparisons of Lemma <a href="#rt:weight-comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="rt:weight-comparison">102</a>, by a fixed finite direct sum of ideal hybrid cylinder states. Their summed energy is at most $\delta^{-C\gamma}e_L$, each regularity is at most $\delta^{-C\gamma}\kappa f_*^{1-\eta}$, and their assignments satisfy Equation <a href="#eq:endlift" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:endlift">[eq:endlift]</a>, with arbitrarily small total additive errors. The exponent $C\gamma$ is independent of the finite-power exponent of $H^{-1}$.
  - Explanation: In the stated normal quantum regime, finite direct sums freeze the base as exact cylinder indices while retaining the normal quantum propagator and controlled assignment comparisons.
- **claim-round-cone-growth-bound** (bound, [source](#stmt-thm-round)): For every $0<\eta<1$, the round-cone experiments satisfy $$\Gamma_{\mathrm{cl},\mathrm{round}}\le 100\eta, \qquad \Gamma_{\mathrm{wav},\mathrm{round}}\le 100\eta.$$ The same upper exponent bounds hold with a fixed finite list of admissible row contractions, with arbitrary separable Hilbert multiplicity, and with the finite-power support and error conventions of the round-cone model.
  - Explanation: Classical and wave round-cone growth exponents obey the stated regularity loss, also with fixed finite row contractions and separable Hilbert multiplicity.
- **claim-classical-round-test-volume** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-rt-test-volume)): Normalize the parent length to one and let $\nu$ be a classical phase measure supported in a fixed bounded box of $(b,y,A)$, with Lebesgue density at most $L_0$. Uniformly in the centers and coefficients of every admissible round or hyperquadric test, $$\label{eq:rt-test-volume} \frac{\nu(\text{test})}{r^4f^{1-\eta}} \le C L_0\min(r^2,r^{-3})f^\eta.$$ The constant depends only on the support box and the fixed test coefficient bound.
  - Explanation: A bounded phase density controls normalized test mass uniformly in centers and coefficients through small-width and large-width volume bounds.
- **claim-saturated-wave-angular-uncertainty** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-rt-planck)): In the wave contradiction, a homogeneous saturating family at any positive-depth cut $j$ satisfies $$\frac{r_j}{d_{\ell_j}}=s^{o(1)}. \tag{round-Pl}\label{eq:round-Pl}$$ After normalizing the terminal angular width to $r_1=1$, it follows that $$H=s^{1+o(1)},\qquad u(a)=\frac{1-a}{2},\qquad r_a=s^{u(a)+o(1)}. \tag{round-u}\label{eq:round-u}$$
  - Explanation: Strict wave saturation forces angular width to the packet uncertainty scale and determines the normalized angular depth profile.
- **claim-round-spatial-readout** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-rt-spatial-readout)): For a free wave with this bounded angular spectrum, $$\Delta^{-1/2}\sum_\lambda m_\lambda^{3/2} \lesssim s^{-o(1)}\int_{\mathcal U}\lVert u(t,b,y)\rVert^3\,dt\,db\,dy +\text{negligible error}. \tag{space-3}\label{eq:space-3}$$ Here $\mathcal U$ can contain the bounded time interval and all space. If the contributing input rows are localized in bounded phase boxes, only their subpower enlarged spacetime region is needed.
  - Explanation: For the specified free wave spectrum, the terminal mass readout is controlled by the spacetime norm, with a localized version for phase-localized inputs.
- **claim-velocity-plane-slab-estimates** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-rt-plane)): There is a universal constant $C$ with the following properties. Let $\lambda>0$ be sufficiently small relative to $\varepsilon$. If $\|\alpha\|^2-4\beta d_0\lesssim\rho^{2\lambda}$, one may choose $0<h'<\lambda h$, inside any prescribed available positive gap, so that $$\Delta^{-1/2}\sum_\lambda m_\lambda^{3/2} \le s^{-o(1)}\sqrt{\kappa_*}\,e_g. \tag{tiny-cap}\label{eq:tiny-cap}$$ In the complementary case choose a fixed $0<h'\le\varepsilon h/20$ inside the available gap, then take $\lambda$ sufficiently small relative to $h'/h$. With $P=\rho^{-\lambda}$, $$\Delta^{-1/2}\sum_\lambda m_\lambda^{3/2} \lesssim s^{-o(1)}P^C\Delta^{-4\eta} \sqrt{\kappa_*}\,e_g. \tag{sec}\label{eq:sec}$$ The estimates hold classically even after further positive restrictions or raywise contractions. For waves they concern the free continuation of the specified input state.
  - Explanation: Near-degenerate velocity sections and transverse sections have separate short-gap readout bounds; the wave statement concerns free continuation of the specified state.
- **claim-round-selected-laws-rarity** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-rt-laws)): For any fixed finite rational list of cuts and names, one can choose the saturated configuration in forward order so that the following properties hold to arbitrarily small exponent errors. At every requested subterminal cut $a$, the selected raw mass and the post-synthesis energy both have size $E_a$. The raw rows have intervalwise regularity at most $s^{-o(1)}\kappa_a$ and are carried on peeling labels with $$\label{eq:rt-weight-count} \sum_{\lambda_a}w_{\lambda_a} \le s^{-o(1)}E_a/\kappa_a.$$ Write $\mathbf P^a$ for their normalized raw row law. If a portion tested at a later selected cut $l$ can only be reached through a set of relative raw mass $q$ at $i<l$, then its relative mass at $l$ is at most $s^{-o(1)}q^{2/3}$, up to negligible error. Consequently a power-rare necessary predecessor remains power-rare at the later law. For classical rays the same conclusion holds at the final assigned law $\mathbf P^1$.
  - Explanation: Forward preserving selections realize energy and regularity benchmarks and transport necessary-predecessor rarity to later selected laws.
- **claim-wave-ancestor-name-stability** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-rt-stability)): At a wave cut $a$, preflatten $C(a,v)$ and $(C(a,v),A_w)$, with $v\le w\le u(a)$. At a later sampled cut $b$ with $w\le u(b)$, the same deterministic exponents hold for their backevaluated names, including after further subpower restrictions of $\mathbf P^b$.
  - Explanation: Preflattened ancestor and angular joint-name exponents persist on later backevaluated wave laws within the stated angular domain.
- **claim-round-entropy-profiles** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-rt-profiles)): Passing to finite-list subsequences and then a diagonal, there are Lipschitz profiles $$\begin{split} D(a,v)&=\lim\left(i_s(C(a,v))- \log_{1/s}(e/\kappa)\right),\\ J(a,v,w)&=\lim i_s(A_w\mid C(a,v)),\qquad v\le w\le u(a), \end{split} \tag{prof}\label{eq:prof}$$ in probability on each of the valid measuring laws. For classical rays only $D(a,0)$ and $J(a,0,w)$, $0\le w\le1$, are used. The wave excess satisfies $$E(a,v):=D(a,v)-4v-(p+d)a\ge0, \qquad E(a,u(a))=0. \tag{excess}\label{eq:excess}$$ Classically $D(a,0)\ge(p+d)a$ and $D(1,0)\le p+d$. Furthermore $0\le J(a,v,w)\le2(w-v)$, $J$ is nonincreasing in $a$ for fixed $v,w$, and in the wave case $$\label{eq:rt-superadditive} J(a,v,w)\ge J(a,v,x)+J(a,x,w),\qquad v<x<w.$$ Every bounded-branching score increment in these assertions has the same limit in expectation as in probability.
  - Explanation: Finite-list subsequences yield compatible Lipschitz profiles with nonnegative excess, boundary equality, angular capacities and superadditive increments.
- **claim-classical-round-angular-memory** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-rt-memory)): For classical rays, at any fixed root name $C(a,0)$ and any $0<w<1$, the typical conditional surprise of $A_w$ is at least $(3-p)w-o(1)$. Consequently $$\label{eq:rt-classical-m} m:=3-p=2-2d+2\Gamma\in(0,2].$$
  - Explanation: Classical positive transport and predecessor coverings give the lower conditional angular surprise and the associated memory parameter range.
- **claim-round-time-spread** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-rt-time)): For every fixed finite list $0<z\le1$, $$\label{eq:rt-time-score} i_\rho(\theta_z\mid C,Y_\#)\ge dz-o(1)$$ typically. The statement is power-robust at each strict tolerance, including after subpower restrictions of the measuring law.
  - Explanation: Causal multiplicity bounds exclude overly concentrated time names and remain robust under qualified later measuring-law restrictions.
- **claim-conditional-plane-removal** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-rt-slab-removal)): At the query in Equation <a href="#eq:query" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:query">[eq:query]</a>, fix $\varepsilon>0$. In the wave case one may restrict $\mathbf P^b$ by subpower mass; in the classical case no additional restriction is necessary. The resulting laws have all the preceding robust score properties and satisfy, typically in $(C,C')$, $$\label{eq:rt-plane-nonconcentration} \sup_{\Pi}\mathbf P\{\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(V(Z),\Pi)\le\rho^\varepsilon \mid C,C'\}\longrightarrow0,$$ where $\Pi$ ranges over affine planes in $\mathbb R^3$. These choices are made before any conditional product sampling.
  - Explanation: Before conditional product sampling, wave row laws can be restricted by subpower mass to eliminate conditional velocity-plane concentration while preserving robust profiles.
- **claim-superadditive-interval-density** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-rt-interval-density)): Let $J(x,y)$ be continuous for $x\le y$ in a compact interval, with $0\le J(x,y)\le M(y-x)$ and $J(x,z)\ge J(x,y)+J(y,z)$. Then there is a measurable $m\in[0,M]$ such that $$\lim_{r\downarrow0}\frac{J(x,x+r)}r=m(x) \quad\hbox{for almost every }x.$$ Applied to the wave profiles, there is a jointly measurable version $m(a,v)\in[0,2]$, nonincreasing in $a$ for fixed $v$, for which $$\label{eq:rt-angular-tangent} \frac{J(a,v,v+zh)}h\longrightarrow z m(a,v)$$ at almost every interior $(a,v)$, for each fixed $z>0$.
  - Explanation: A continuous bounded superadditive interval function has an almost-everywhere diagonal density; the wave profiles admit a jointly measurable monotone version.
- **claim-round-dyadic-stationarity** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-rt-stationarity)): At almost every interior wave point, and almost every classical depth $a$ with $v=0$, along $h=2^{-n}\downarrow0$ one has $$J(a,v,v+Kh)-J(a+Kh,v,v+Kh)=o(h). \tag{stat}\label{eq:stat}$$
  - Explanation: Monotonicity and summable integrated decrements give negligible time change of angular information along dyadic tangent gaps.
- **claim-wave-width-derivative** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-rt-width-derivative)): At almost every interior wave point, $$\partial_vD\le m+o_T-d+1. \tag{rv}\label{eq:rv}$$
  - Explanation: Angular and position names determine width refinement after paying for time spread and the remaining vertical precision.
- **claim-round-outgoing-entropy** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-rt-outgoing)): Use the exponent data $d,p,\Gamma$ of Equation <a href="#eq:rt-pd" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:rt-pd">[eq:rt-pd]</a>. For almost every classical depth $a\in(0,1)$ at which $D(a,0)$ is differentiable and Lemma <a href="#lem:rt-stationarity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:rt-stationarity">116</a> applies, put $o_T=\partial_aD(a,0)$ and $m=3-p$. For waves, let $(a,v)$ be almost every interior point with $0<a<1$ and $0<v<(1-a)/2$ at which $D$ is differentiable and Lemmas <a href="#lem:rt-interval-density" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:rt-interval-density">115</a> and <a href="#lem:rt-stationarity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:rt-stationarity">116</a> apply, and put $o_T=\partial_aD(a,v)$ and $m=m(a,v)$. In either case, $$o_T\ge4d+\min(1-d,m/2). \tag{round-out}\label{eq:round-out}$$
  - Explanation: Transverse conditional pins and planar incidences force the outgoing depth-entropy lower bound in the specified classical and interior wave regimes.
- **claim-two-direction-descent-impossibility** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-rt-descent)): Let $\Omega=\{(t,v):0<t<1,\ 0<v<t/2\}$. Suppose that $E$ is locally Lipschitz, nonnegative, and has zero trace on $v=t/2$. Let $m$ be measurable and nondecreasing in $t$ at each fixed $v$, with this condition allowed outside a null set of $v$. If $c>0$ and $q\in\mathbb R$, the following pair of almost everywhere inequalities is impossible: $$E_t+\tfrac12E_v\le-c\quad\hbox{where }m\le q, \qquad E_t\le-c\quad\hbox{where }m\ge q.$$
  - Explanation: A nonnegative locally Lipschitz excess with zero boundary trace cannot satisfy the indicated moving and vertical decreases with a monotone threshold field.
- **claim-physical-annular-smoothing** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-phys-annular)): For every $\delta>0$, $$\lVert W_Hg\rVert_{L^3(\mathbb R^3\times[1,2])} \le C_\delta H^{-\delta}\lVert g\rVert_{L^3(\mathbb R^3)}. \label{eq:phys-annular-estimate}$$
  - Explanation: Uniformly smooth annular half-wave multipliers satisfy the critical estimate with an arbitrarily small positive frequency loss.
- **claim-initial-slice-packet-localization** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-phys-initial-kernel)): Fix $\gamma_0>0$ and put $\Lambda=H^{-\gamma_0}$. The operator $g\mapsto V_1v(T)$ can be truncated to the following relation between an input point $z=(z_\perp,z_3)\in K$ and a row $(A,b,y)$: $$\begin{aligned} \|b-z_\perp-(T-z_3)A\|&\le C\Lambda\sqrt H,\notag\\ \|y+z_3-(T-z_3)\|A\|^2 -2A\cdot(b-z_\perp-(T-z_3)A)\|&\le C\Lambda H. \label{eq:phys-predecessor-relation} \end{aligned}$$ For every $N$, the discarded operator has norm at most $C_NH^N$ from $L^2(K)$ to the row space. The constant is independent of any regularity test subsequently imposed on the output rows. The kernel vanishes unless $\|A\|\le A_0+C_\psi\sqrt H$, where $C_\psi$ is a radius containing the support of the fixed angular window $\psi$.
  - Explanation: A truncation independent of the later test localizes the initial-slice analysis kernel with arbitrarily small discarded operator norm and bounded row angles.
- **claim-physical-predecessor-volume** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-phys-predecessor-volume)): Fix $0<\eta<1$. Consider any round-cone regularity test at time $T$ and length $1$, of angular width $r$ and relative thickness $f$, where $0<f\le1$ and $rf\ge\sqrt H$; for a round test set $f=1$. Let $E$ be the set of $z\in K$ related by Equation <a href="#eq:phys-predecessor-relation" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:phys-predecessor-relation">[eq:phys-predecessor-relation]</a> to some row of the test whose angular coordinate satisfies $\|A\|\le A_0+C_\psi\sqrt H$. There is a fixed $C_1$ such that $$\|E\|\le C\Lambda^{C_1}r^4 f^{1-\eta}. \label{eq:phys-predecessor-volume}$$ The estimate is uniform in the center, $r$, and $f$ of the test.
  - Explanation: The physical initial slice intersects test predecessors in a volume controlled by the round test weight and a fixed localization enlargement.
- **claim-physical-input-regularity** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-phys-input-regularity)): Fix $0<\eta<1$ as in Definition <a href="#rt:regularity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="rt:regularity">91</a>. For every $\gamma>0$, the state in Equation <a href="#eq:phys-round-state" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:phys-round-state">[eq:phys-round-state]</a> has input regularity constant $$\kappa=C_{\eta,\gamma}H^{-\gamma}B^2 \label{eq:phys-kappa}$$ at each of the bounded starting times $T$. Under Equation <a href="#eq:phys-energy-range" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:phys-energy-range">[eq:phys-energy-range]</a>, it also satisfies the polynomial-size and negligible-tail hypotheses of the round-wave experiment with terminal length $s=H$.
  - Explanation: Initial kernel localization and predecessor volume give full round-wave input regularity; the stated energy range also ensures polynomial sizes and negligible tails.
- **claim-terminal-physical-synthesis** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-phys-synthesis)): Let $v$ be the wave in Equation <a href="#eq:phys-round-state" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:phys-round-state">[eq:phys-round-state]</a>, and let $\Omega$ be a fixed bounded subset of $(b,y)$ space. At each left endpoint $T_j=T+jH$ in $[T,T+1]$, use a plateau analysis of length $H$, and group its row masses into spatial $H$-grid cubes. Restrict to a fixed enlargement of $\Omega$, and denote the resulting masses by $m_{j,Q}$. They are admissible round-test assignments with weights bounded above and below by positive constants. For every $0<\sigma<1$ and $N$, $$\int_T^{T+1}\int_\Omega \|v\|^3 \le C_\sigma H^{-C_4\sigma}H^{-1/2} \sum_{j,Q}m_{j,Q}^{3/2} +C_{N,\sigma}H^N e^{3/2}. \label{eq:phys-synthesis}$$ Here $H$ is dyadic, so the time partition is exact.
  - Explanation: Plateau row masses in terminal spatial cubes form admissible assignments controlling the localized physical spacetime norm with a small power loss and negligible error.
- **claim-full-positive-smoothing-range** (bound, [source](#stmt-cor-full-range)): For every $2<p<\infty$ and $\alpha>\max\{0,1-3/p\}$, $$\lVert Uf\rVert_{L^p(\mathbb R^3\times[1,2])} \le C_{p,\alpha}\lVert J^\alpha f\rVert_{L^p(\mathbb R^3)} \qquad(f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)). \label{eq:phys-full-range}$$
  - Explanation: Interpolation and frequency summation extend the critical estimate to the full strict positive-regularity Euclidean range.
- **claim-maximal-half-wave-convergence** (bound, [source](#stmt-cor-wave-maximal)): Let $3\le p<\infty$ and $s>1-2/p$. Then $$\label{eq:wave-maximal} \left\\|\sup_{0<t<1}\|Uf(\cdot,t)\|\right\\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^3)} \le C_{p,s}\lVert J^s f\rVert_{L^p(\mathbb R^3)} \qquad(f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)).$$ The family has a bounded maximal extension to $W^{s,p}(\mathbb R^3)$, and in that extension every $f\in W^{s,p}(\mathbb R^3)$ satisfies $$\label{eq:wave-initial-limit} \lim_{t\downarrow0}Uf(x,t)=f(x) \quad\text{for almost every }x\in\mathbb R^3.$$
  - Explanation: The stated Sobolev regularity yields a bounded finite-time maximal extension and almost-everywhere recovery of the initial data.
- **claim-maximal-bochner-riesz-summation** (bound, [source](#stmt-thm-br-maximal)): Let $3\le p<\infty$ and $\delta>1-3/p$. Then $$\label{eq:br-maximal} \lVert B_*^\delta f\rVert_{L^p(\mathbb R^3)} \le C_{p,\delta}\lVert f\rVert_{L^p(\mathbb R^3)} \qquad(f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)).$$ The family has a bounded maximal extension to $L^p(\mathbb R^3)$, and in that extension every $f\in L^p(\mathbb R^3)$ satisfies $$\label{eq:br-ae} \lim_{R\to\infty}B_R^\delta f(x)=f(x) \quad\text{for almost every }x\in\mathbb R^3.$$ In particular, every $\delta>0$ is allowed when $p=3$.
  - Explanation: Local smoothing implies strong maximal Bochner–Riesz bounds and almost-everywhere summation in the stated strict order range.
- **claim-strict-nonmaximal-bochner-riesz** (bound, [source](#stmt-cor-br-nonmaximal)): For $1\le p\le\infty$, with $1/\infty=0$, set $$\delta_{\mathrm{BR}}(p) =\max\left\{3\left\|\frac1p-\frac12\right\|-\frac12,0\right\}.$$ If $\delta>\delta_{\mathrm{BR}}(p)$, the operators $B_R^\delta$ extend boundedly to $L^p(\mathbb R^3)$ with a bound uniform in $R>0$: $$\label{eq:br-nonmaximal} \lVert B_R^\delta f\rVert_{L^p(\mathbb R^3)} \le C_{p,\delta}\lVert f\rVert_{L^p(\mathbb R^3)}.$$
  - Explanation: Individual Bochner–Riesz means extend boundedly throughout the full strict nonmaximal range with a constant uniform in the radius.

        "anchor": "stmt-cyl-matched-chain",

        "anchor": "stmt-cyl-profiles",
        "exact_quote": "The preceding minima have feasible finite values. Normalize $r_1=f_1=1$. Along successively finer matched meshes one may extract Lipschitz limits $$\\label{cyl:profile-definition}\n u(i)=\\lim\\log_s r_i,\\qquad n(i)=\\lim\\log_s f_i,\\qquad\n b_t(i)=n(i)-tu(i)\\quad(t=1,2).$$ Here $u,n$ vanish at $1$ and $u$ is nonincreasing, hence nonnegative. In the strict-gap hybrid case, $n(i)=(1-i)/2$. Along any connecting chain from $i$ to $j$, $$\\tag{A}\\label{eq:A}\n \\begin{split}\n |\\beta_i(T_j)-\\beta_j(T_j)|\n        &\\le s^{\\min_{[i,j]}b_2-o(1)},\\\\\n |K_i-K_j|\n        &\\le s^{\\min_{k\\in[i,j]}(b_2(k)-k)-o(1)},\\\\\n |P_i(F)-P_j(F)|&\\le s^{\\min_{[i,j]}b_1-o(1)}.\n \\end{split}$$ One may also impose the individual curvature bound $$\\tag{B}\\label{eq:B}\n |\\beta_i(T_i)|+\\ell_i|K_i|\n        \\le s^{\\min(-c,\\min_{[i,1]}b_2)-o(1)}.$$",
        "source_id": "PM-079.1"
      },

        "anchor": "stmt-cyl-affine",
        "exact_quote": "If at least one relevant minimal cost is positive, one can pass to extremizing documented configurations with $$\\tag{F}\\label{eq:F}\n u(i)=J(1-i),\\quad J\\ge0,\\qquad\n \\begin{cases}\n b_2(i)=q(i-1),&c>0,\\\\\n b_1(i)=c_1(i-1),&c=0<c_1.\n \\end{cases}$$ For $c\\ne1$, $q=c$. In the latter option, $$|\\beta_1(T_1)|\\le s^{-1-o(1)},\\qquad\n s|K_l|\\le s^{-o(1)}\\quad\\hbox{at every gate }l.$$ For $0<c\\le1$ and $q=c$, one has $\\ell_l|K_l|\\le s^{b_2(l)-o(1)}$, and the own-time values $\\beta_i(T_i),\\beta_l(T_l)$ on forward connections differ by at most $s^{b_2(i)-o(1)}$. The linear alternative retains its individual curvature bounds and the center-derivative comparison at precision $s^{b_1(i)-o(1)}$.*\n\n*All relevant terminal minimal costs, gate counts, read-mass bounds, Equations <a href=\"#eq:M\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:M\">[eq:M]</a> and <a href=\"#eq:A\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:A\">[eq:A]</a>, and the permission to insert ordinary regularization persist.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-cyl-borel-paths",
        "exact_quote": "Fix an inner scale, a finite stack of cuts, a finite query list, and a correspondence truncation.*\n\n1.  *The side and row data admit standard Borel codes in which the primitive correspondences, time ownership, physical masks, analyzed-state essential supports, and assignment supports have Borel versions. All energetically active paths occur in a Borel finite-path relation. Its coordinate projections, including completion events, are analytic and hence measurable in the completion of every Borel row law (Bertsekas and Shreve, n.d., sec. 3, Theorem 2).*\n\n2.  *For an analytic row event $A$ and a finite Borel row law $\\mu$, there are Borel versions $A^-\\subset A\\subset A^+$ with $\\mu(A^+\\setminus A^-)=0$. For a pre-synthesis mask, $\\mu$ is the *full analyzed row-energy law* $\\|V_i g_i\\|^2$ in the active intervals, before fractional assignments. An assigned law suffices only for a terminal readout. An inner version of a completion event retains a completion for every one of its rows.*\n\n3.  *Let $B$ be a Borel inner version of a marked end-row event, intersected with the current end-state positive-norm set $H_j$; it has the same full analyzed end-row mass as the marked event. Let $S$ consist of all predecessors of $B$ under the unrestricted truncated geometric correspondence from the starting gate to the marked gate. This relation uses the current starting-state essential support and the pre-existing intermediate physical masks. It does not impose the success event that selected $B$ again, or the original state’s intermediate supports. The set $S$ is analytic and has Borel versions $$S^-\\subset S\\subset S^+,\n     \\qquad \\mu(S^+\\setminus S^-)=0$$ under the full analyzed starting-row energy law. Thus $S^+$ contains every geometric predecessor pointwise. Synthesis restricted to $S^+$ and $S^-$ gives identical states, and the two restrictions have equal analyzed input energy. This assertion concerns the physical state; a completing witness may have zero conditional probability under a separate path law.*\n\n4.  *With finitely many possible witness bins, the marked end rows may first be disjointized by bin and given Borel inner versions in $H_j$. Each retained row still has a completion in its chosen bin. Form each bin’s predecessor set by the unrestricted correspondence in <span class=\"upright\">(iii)</span>. If path concatenation places this set in a Borel allowed starting-bin set $P_b$, both predecessor versions may be chosen inside $P_b$. The original starting-bin partition and its overlap count are then preserved. Use the outer versions for pointwise locality and the inner versions for physical restrictions and input-energy accounting.*\n\n5.  *The versions may be chosen jointly in side and row coordinates, and simultaneously for any fixed finite or countable family of full analyzed and comparison laws. After a new restriction or a row law not dominated by those laws is formed, choose versions under that law before the next projection. Complements of analytic events are used only as completed-measurable events, or given Borel inner versions before entering another path relation. Conditional assertions obtained by disintegration hold for almost every side value; a uniform assertion requires a separate finite-grid or quantitative exceptional-side argument.",

        "exact_quote": "Use an affine documented configuration as in Equation <a href=\"#eq:F\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:F\">[eq:F]</a>, with ordinary regularity imposed immediately before the relevant gates.         "anchor": "stmt-low-likelihood",
        "exact_quote": "For arbitrary additional side information $D'$ and $\\epsilon>0$, $$i_\\rho(U\\mid D)\\geq i_\\rho(U\\mid D,D')-\\epsilon\n \\tag{LP}\\label{eq:LP}$$ outside a set of probability at most $\\rho^\\epsilon$. If $I(U;D'\\mid D)=o(\\log(1/\\rho))$, the difference of these scores tends to zero in probability. More precisely, if the sampled $U$ belongs on an event $E$ to a list $\\mathcal L(V,D)$ of at most $\\rho^{-b}$ names, then $$\\mathbb P\\bigl(E\\cap\\{i_\\rho(U\\mid D)>\n              i_\\rho(V\\mid D)+b+\\epsilon\\}\\bigr)\n \\leq\\rho^\\epsilon.$$ If $V$ instead belongs to a list indexed by $(U,D)$, reverse $U,V$ in this comparison. Thus a change of discrete names by such lists costs at most $b+\\epsilon$ in the indicated direction. The exceptional probability is measured on $E$ under the original law; no conditioning on $E$ is implicit. Finally, restricting the law to an event of probability bounded below preserves any fixed finite collection of normalized scores up to an error tending to zero in probability under the restricted law.",

        "anchor": "stmt-names-memory",
        "exact_quote": "Put $k_0=1-d$ and $$L_{\\rm raw}=\\max\\{1,(1+Q)/2,1+C_{\\rm rate}\\},\\qquad\n (Q,C_{\\rm rate})=\n \\begin{cases}(q,q-J),&\\text{curvature families},\\\\\n (0,c_1),&\\text{pure linear}.\n \\end{cases}$$ Whenever the left label comparison in Proposition <a href=\"#names:canonical-entropy\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"names:canonical-entropy\">51</a>(iii) applies at $v=u(j)$, the angular trace satisfies $$m(a,v)\\geq\n \\frac{k_0+2\\Gamma+\\eta(L_{\\rm raw}-1)}{L_{\\rm raw}}.$$ Fix a classical depth $j$, and let $\\lambda_j$ denote the random label encountered there on the final assigned law. Define $R_j(v)=\\lim H_s(X^{(v)}\\mid\\lambda_j)$, with conditional entropy averaged over that label random variable. Under the small right-excess comparison, $m(a,v)\\geq R_j'(v)$ almost everywhere. At typical classical $j$ with $C_{\\rm rate}>0$, the following improvements are available:*\n\n1.  *If $p_*(j)>b_1(j)$, with the extra prediction persisting immediately to the left, replace $L_{\\rm raw}$ by $\\max\\{1,(1+Q)/2\\}$.*\n\n2.  *If $Q\\leq1$ and $0<C_{\\rm rate}<1$, an additional lower bound is $k_0+2\\Gamma-C_{\\rm rate}\\nu(j)$, where $\\nu$ is the mixed trace for the raw derivative, side $y_0$, and graph $B=b_1$.",
      "explanation": "Label prediction converts memory rarity into lower angular trace bounds, with stronger classical bounds under additional coefficient prediction or mixed-trace control.",

        "anchor": "stmt-names-separation",
        "exact_quote": "In an equality quadratic family with $c>0$, the conditional $(\\theta,r)$ law for an admissible side avoids arbitrary affine lines with a positive power.         "anchor": "stmt-names-replica-budgets",
        "exact_quote": "At almost every interior admissible root there are arbitrarily small tangent gaps with sufficiently accurate preceding experiments such that, for any fixed finite collection of queries, $$I_\\delta(F_{\\leq p'};\\boldsymbol\\Xi\\mid C_*)=o(1).\n \\tag{vb}\\label{eq:vb}$$ Define a fiber read $Q_i$, at a sufficiently large finite depth relative to still finer stored marks, by binning $$B+\\theta_iX,\\quad Y+\\theta_iX^2,\\quad D_0'+\\theta_iN,\n \\quad\n \\begin{cases}\n P-2r_iX,\\ N-PX+r_iX^2,&\\text{quadratic},\\\\\n N-r_iX,&\\text{linear}.\n \\end{cases}$$ Then $$\\begin{split}\n I_\\delta(X_{\\leq p'};Q_i,\\boldsymbol\\Xi\\mid C_*)&=o(1),\\\\\n i_\\delta(X_{\\leq p'}\\mid C_*)&=m(a,v)p'+o(1)\n                         \\quad\\text{in probability}.\n \\end{split}\n \\tag{fib}\\label{eq:fib}$$ At a fixed boundary root with one observation, only the consequence of <a href=\"#eq:ng\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:ng\">[eq:ng]</a> for adding that observation and its fiber read is asserted; neither <a href=\"#eq:vb\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:vb\">[eq:vb]</a> nor an interior angular trace is asserted there.",

        "exact_quote": "One may resample the common side and its phase successively from their joint law conditional on $C_*,\\boldsymbol\\Xi,Q_i$, optionally retaining an angular prefix bin. Each leg preserves the joint marked marginal. Fine angular increments of the new endpoint have negligible normalized information from the preceding history beyond that already present in $C_*$ and the retained prefix. For a leg with $A=\\Delta X$, its increments satisfy, up to arbitrarily fine specified errors, $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\Delta B&=-\\theta_i A,&\n \\Delta Y&=-\\theta_i(2XA+A^2),&\n \\Delta D_0'&=-\\theta_i\\Delta N,\\\\\n \\Delta P&=2r_iA,&\n \\Delta N&=PA+r_iA^2&&\\text{(quadratic)},\\\\\n &&\\Delta N&=r_iA&&\\text{(linear)}.\n\\end{aligned}\n\\tag{leg}\\label{eq:leg}$$ For a finite walk without a retained prefix, the new angular draws have joint negligible information relative to independent draws given $C_*$, including relative to the starting phase and all marks.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-names-score-limits",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose a finite collection of name arrays $A_q$, with depths in a bounded interval, has the following properties. Coarser names are determined from finer names up to lists of size $\\rho^{-o(1)}$, and, conditionally on $A_q,D$, the name $A_{q'}$, $q'\\ge q$, has at most $\\rho^{-K(q'-q)-o(1)}$ possible values. The same bounds hold for the joint arrays under consideration, and their total range sizes are at most a fixed power of $\\rho^{-1}$. Then, after a subsequence, the scores at countably many fixed queries have a joint distributional limit with these properties:*\n\n1.  *Cumulative scores are nonnegative, nondecreasing, and Lipschitz in each named-variable refinement argument, with conditioning held fixed and with the corresponding branching constant. They extend from rational queries to real queries.*\n\n\n2.  *The chain rule holds, and adding conditioning can only decrease a conditional score. In particular, for $r\\le r'\\le a\\le b$, whenever $F_r$ is a nested conditioning array, $$\\begin{aligned}\n     &i(A_b\\mid F_{r'},D)-i(A_a\\mid F_{r'},D)\\notag\\\\\n     &\\hspace{15mm}\\le\n     i(A_b\\mid F_r,D)-i(A_a\\mid F_r,D).\n     \\label{names:score-increment-monotonicity}\n    \\end{aligned}$$ Here and below $i$ without a scale denotes a limiting random score.*\n\n3.  *Mutual determination with exponent-zero lists identifies the corresponding limiting scores. All these statements hold simultaneously almost surely for the countable family of queries.",

      },

They extend from rational queries to real queries.*\n\n\n2.  *The chain rule holds, and adding conditioning can only decrease a conditional score. In particular, for $r\\le r'\\le a\\le b$, whenever $F_r$ is a nested conditioning array, $$\\begin{aligned}\n     &i(A_b\\mid F_{r'},D)-i(A_a\\mid F_{r'},D)\\notag\\\\\n     &\\hspace{15mm}\\le\n     i(A_b\\mid F_r,D)-i(A_a\\mid F_r,D).\n     \\label{names:score-increment-monotonicity}\n    \\end{aligned}$$ Here and below $i$ without a scale denotes a limiting random score.*\n\n3.  *Mutual determination with exponent-zero lists identifies the corresponding limiting scores.       "exact_statement": "Suppose a finite collection of name arrays $A_q$, with depths in a bounded interval, has the following properties. Coarser names are determined from finer names up to lists of size $\\rho^{-o(1)}$, and, conditionally on $A_q,D$, the name $A_{q'}$, $q'\\ge q$, has at most $\\rho^{-K(q'-q)-o(1)}$ possible values. The same bounds hold for the joint arrays under consideration, and their total range sizes are at most a fixed power of $\\rho^{-1}$. Then, after a subsequence, the scores at countably many fixed queries have a joint distributional limit with these properties:*\n\n1.  *Cumulative scores are nonnegative, nondecreasing, and Lipschitz in each named-variable refinement argument, with conditioning held fixed and with the corresponding branching constant. They extend from rational queries to real queries.*\n\n\n2.  *The chain rule holds, and adding conditioning can only decrease a conditional score. In particular, for $r\\le r'\\le a\\le b$, whenever $F_r$ is a nested conditioning array, $$\\begin{aligned}\n     &i(A_b\\mid F_{r'},D)-i(A_a\\mid F_{r'},D)\\notag\\\\\n     &\\hspace{15mm}\\le\n     i(A_b\\mid F_r,D)-i(A_a\\mid F_r,D).\n     \\label{names:score-increment-monotonicity}\n    \\end{aligned}$$ Here and below $i$ without a scale denotes a limiting random score.*\n\n3.  *Mutual determination with exponent-zero lists identifies the corresponding limiting scores. All these statements hold simultaneously almost surely for the countable family of queries.",

        "anchor": "stmt-names-projection-rule",
        "exact_quote": "Let $0\\le S\\le2$, $0<b\\le1$, and $\\Delta\\downarrow0$. Let $Z$ be a bounded planar source, $W$ a record determining a direction $g(W)$, and $D$ common side data. Assume $$I(Z;W\\mid D)=o(\\log(1/\\Delta)).\n \\label{names:score-projection-budget}$$ Suppose there is an event $G$ of probability bounded below such that its unnormalized conditional marginals obey, for every needed ball and interval of radius $\\Delta\\le r\\le1$, $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\mathbb P(G,\\ Z\\in B(z,r)\\mid D)&\\le\\Delta^{-o(1)}r^S,\\notag\\\\\n \\mathbb P(G,\\ g(W)\\in J(r)\\mid D)&\\le\\Delta^{-o(1)}r^b.\n \\label{names:score-projection-masses}\n\\end{aligned}$$ For each $D,W$, let $\\mathcal I(D,W)$ be a list of at most $\\Delta^{-x-o(1)}$ intervals of length $O(\\Delta)$, and suppose that on $G$ the projection of $Z$ in direction $g(W)$ belongs to their union, up to $O(\\Delta)$ error. Then $$x\\ge\\min\\{S,(S+b)/2,1\\}.\n \\label{names:score-projection-conclusion}$$ The assertion is a strict-error statement: a fixed strict deficit is impossible if all preceding exponent losses and the information ratio are sufficiently small. Consequently a sufficiently fine finite grid of prefix radii suffices, and errors of size $\\Delta^{1-o(1)}$ in directions, representatives, or output resolution are allowed. The same conclusion holds with $c_\\Delta=\\mathbb P(G)$ tending to zero, provided $$\\log(1/c_\\Delta)=o(\\log(1/\\Delta)),\\qquad\n I(Z;W\\mid D)=o(c_\\Delta\\log(1/\\Delta)).$$",
        "source_id": "PM-079.1"
      },

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-names-radial-dichotomy",
        "exact_quote": "Let $\\xi_i=(\\theta_i,r_i)$ and $\\xi_j=(\\theta_j,r_j)$ be conditionally independent, identically distributed planar marks given $Z$. Suppose their bounded-depth records obey the preceding score calculus, and their time marginals have prefix mass exponent at least $d>0$ given $Z$, with $d\\leq1$. More precisely, at every prescribed finite collection of depths, discarding a set of vanishing average probability makes the unnormalized conditional time-interval bounds hold with exponent $d$ and arbitrarily small losses. Assume <a href=\"#eq:RW\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:RW\">[eq:RW]</a>.*\n\n\n*Trim at the required depths to measures $\\mu_Z$ dominated by the conditional mark laws.         "anchor": "stmt-names-parent-direction-transfer",
        "exact_quote": "Let $P$ be a law of a side variable $Z$, finitely many full records $\\boldsymbol V$, and a finite auxiliary name $A$. Suppose that the record marginal is conditionally iid given $Z=z$, with law $\\nu_z$. Each record has a bounded planar projection $\\pi_z(V_i)$; write $\\mu_z=(\\pi_z)_\\#\\nu_z$ for its law. The full record may retain additional entries, including a stored curvature slope. Let $S$ be a function of $Z$, and set $$R(dZ,d\\boldsymbol V,dA)\n   =P(dZ,d\\boldsymbol V)P(dA\\mid S).$$ Assume $\\operatorname{KL}(P\\Vert R)=o(\\log(1/\\delta))$. Choose distinct records $V_x,V_y$, and write $x=\\pi_z(V_x)$, $y=\\pi_z(V_y)$. Let $K$ be the depth-$b$ parent cell of $y$, with representative $c_K$, where $b>0$. For parents of positive mass put $\\mu_z^K=\\mu_z|_K/\\mu_z(K)$. The common data are $$D=(Z,K,A,\\text{the held full records other than }V_x,V_y).$$ Fix $t>0$ sufficiently small compared with $b$, and a finite grid of radii $r=\\delta^{\\sigma t}$, $0<\\sigma\\leq1$. Let $T_z$ be a measurable trimming set in the full record space and put $\\mu_z^T=(\\pi_z)_\\#(\\nu_z|_{T_z})$. In particular the trimming may depend only on the planar projection. Let $W_y=\\psi_D(\\pi_z(V_y))$ be a finite Borel source name in the tested prefix family. Under $R$, its conditional law given $D$ is the image of $\\mu_z^K$ under $\\psi_D$; in applications it is a bin of the rescaled child increment of the moving mark in $K$. On an event $G$, suppose that $V_x\\in T_z$, that $\\lvert x-y\\rvert\\geq\\delta^\\chi$ with $b-\\chi>t$, and that the original witness lines satisfy the tested bounds $$\\mu_z^T(N_{Cr}(\\mathfrak l(x,y)))\n       \\leq C\\delta^{-\\varepsilon t}r^{d-\\varepsilon}.$$ Here the fixed enlargement constants needed below are included among the finite tests. Then, with $g_K(x)$ the direction from $c_K$ to $x$, $$R(G,\\ g_K(x)\\in J(r)\\mid D)\n       \\leq C\\delta^{-\\varepsilon t}r^{d-\\varepsilon}\n \\label{names:parent-direction-bound}$$ for every tested direction interval $J(r)$. A fixed swap or sign change of its coordinate representation preserves the assertion.*\n\n*After deleting a set of $P$-probability tending to zero, the corresponding unnormalized conditional bound under $P$ holds with factor $C\\delta^{-3\\varepsilon t}$. Source prefix bounds for $W_y$ supplied by the original conditional law $\\mu_z(\\cdot\\mid K)$, with their own source trimming when needed, transfer in the same way. Moreover, $$I_P(W_y;V_x\\mid D)\n       \\leq\\operatorname{KL}(P\\Vert R)\n       =o(\\log(1/\\delta^t)).$$ All assertions fix $b,t$, the finite grid, and the tested positive-probability event before sending the information error to zero. No lower bound for $\\mu_z(K)$ is required.",

      },

        "anchor": "stmt-names-radial-low-product",
        "exact_quote": "Fix $0<d\\leq1$. There is a constant $C_d$ with the following property, for every fixed $\\epsilon>0$ and all sufficiently small $\\Delta>0$ depending on $\\epsilon$. Let $\\mu$ have mass at most one and time marginal $$\\mu\\{(\\theta,r):\\theta\\in I\\}\n           \\leq\\Delta^{-\\epsilon}|I|^d\n \\quad(\\Delta\\leq|I|\\leq1).$$ Fix a pin $x=(\\theta_x,r_x)$ in the same fixed bounded set, and let $W_x$ be any subrelation of points $y=(\\theta_y,r_y)$ for which $$|\\theta_y-\\theta_x|,\\ |r_y-r_x|\\geq\\Delta^\\epsilon,\n \\qquad\n \\mu(N_\\Delta(\\mathfrak l(x,y)))\\geq\\Delta^\\epsilon.$$ For $f_x(y)=(\\theta_y-\\theta_x)(r_y-r_x)$, every interval $I$ of length $\\Delta^\\sigma$, $0\\leq\\sigma\\leq1$, satisfies $$\\label{names:radial-low-product-bound}\n \\mu\\{y\\in W_x:f_x(y)\\in I\\}\n            \\leq C_d\\Delta^{d\\sigma-C_d\\epsilon}.$$ Finite grids of prefix hypotheses suffice, with their mesh added to the exponent loss.",
        "source_id": "PM-079.1"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {

        "exact_quote": "In addition to the hypotheses of Proposition <a href=\"#names:radial-dichotomy\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"names:radial-dichotomy\">69</a>, assume the following. The score calculus and the preceding conditional projection rule apply to all fixed finite queries used below. At almost every parent depth $p$, the joint mark increment, conditional on $Z$ and its own parent $\\xi_{j,p}$, has prefix mass exponent at least $d$ on every fixed finite grid of sufficiently small layers $p\\to p+t$. Finally, for every $\\chi>0$, $$\\mathbb P\\bigl\\{|\\theta_i-\\theta_j|\\geq\\rho^\\chi,\n                 \\ |r_i-r_j|\\geq\\rho^\\chi\\bigr\\}\n             \\longrightarrow1.$$ Put $f=(\\theta_j-\\theta_i)(r_j-r_i)$ and $\\mathcal G_+=\\{e_*\\geq d\\}$, $\\mathcal G_0=\\{e_*=0\\}$. Then the limiting cumulative scores satisfy $$\\label{names:radial-high-product}\n i(f_p\\mid Z,\\xi_i)\\geq dp\n       \\quad\\hbox{on }\\mathcal G_+$$ at the tested depths. Here $\\xi_i$ denotes a record stored to a sufficiently large fixed depth, chosen before the $\\rho$-limit.*\n\n*On $\\mathcal G_0$ the following local substitute holds. Any strict violation of a differentiable layer rate on a set of positive probability can be tested at a fixed small layer $t$ on a positive-probability subset where $e(t)<\\epsilon t$. With $\\Delta=\\rho^t$, the unnormalized witness sublaw of $f$, given $Z,\\xi_i$, then has prefix interval bounds of exponent $d$ with loss $O_d(\\epsilon)$, as in <a href=\"#names:radial-low-product-bound\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"names:radial-low-product-bound\">[names:radial-low-product-bound]</a>. The assertion is for a fixed selected layer before earlier approximation and information errors are sent to zero.",

        "exact_quote": "Let $\\delta\\to0$. Let $C$ be a common root name and let side data $\\mathscr Z$ determine $C$, a quadratic phase $F=(X,B,P,Y,N,D)$, and coefficients $(\\beta_F,\\kappa_F)$. The normalized phase, coefficients, and marks have size $\\delta^{-o(1)}$. Conditional on $\\mathscr Z$, draw two independent observations with the same conditional law, whose marks satisfy $$r_i=\\beta_F+\\kappa_F\\theta_i+O(\\delta^{10-o(1)}).\n \\tag{s-line}\\label{eq:s-line}$$ Suppose the following hypotheses hold, with arbitrary fixed strict resolution slack and with exceptional probabilities tending to zero.*\n\n1.  *The conditional score of $\\theta_{i,p+t}$ given $\\mathscr Z,\\theta_{i,p}$ is at least $dt$, for the finitely many queries used below through depth $3$, including queries starting at $0$, where $d>0$.*\n\n2.  *Each observation carries a fiber label $S_i$ such that $(C,S_i)$ determines its marks and the quadratic entries of $Q_i$ in the fiber formulas to single-valued error $\\delta^{10-o(1)}$.*\n\n3.  *Each observation has an output $O_i$ with these recovery properties. The pair $(C,O_i)$ reads $\\theta_i$ to depth $1$, and together with $X_{p+t}$ reads $F_{p+t}$ whenever $0<p<p+t<1$, up to lists of vanishing exponent. If $1<p<p+t<2$ and $t\\ll\\varepsilon,p$, it also predicts $(\\theta_i,r_i)_\\varepsilon$ and, using these coefficients and $F_p$, reads $$K+\\theta_{i,\\varepsilon}J-r_{i,\\varepsilon}H$$ to depth $p+t$. Here $H,J,K$ are the contact forms, evaluated in a fixed positive-depth prefix frame and translated at $F_p$.*\n\n4.  *For each $i$ individually, $$I_\\delta(X_6;S_i\\mid C)=o(1),\\qquad\n     i_\\delta(X_p\\mid C)=M(p)+o(1)$$ in probability at the tested prefixes, where $M$ is deterministic, $M(0)=0$, and $M(p)\\ge g_*p$ for some $g_*>0$.*\n\n\n5.  *Draw $R$ independently from the posterior law of the side and observation given $(C,S_i)$. Its line satisfies $$\\lvert \\kappa_R-\\kappa_F\\rvert\\ge\\delta^\\chi\n     \\quad\\text{with probability tending to one, for every fixed }\\chi>0.\n     \\tag{mis}\\label{eq:mis}$$*\n\n\n*Then $$H_\\delta(O_i\\mid C)\n \\ge d+g_*+2\\min(1,2d)+d+\\min(1,d+g_*)-o(1).\n \\tag{line-time}\\label{eq:line-time}$$ In particular, $g_*\\ge1-2d$ implies the lower bound $2+3d-o(1)$. The finite accuracy constants $6$ and $10$ may be increased.",

        "exact_quote": "Suppose that on an open time interval and in a sufficiently narrow right neighborhood of $v=Jt$ the following hold. The angular rate has its nondecreasing-in-$t$ version.         "anchor": "stmt-rt-saturation",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose $\\Gamma>0$. After realizing these data with arbitrarily small exterior errors, every regularity splitting preserving the terminal functional has limiting dominant regularity and summed energy described by $$\\kappa_a=\\kappa s^{p_0a+o(1)},\\qquad E_a=e s^{-da+o(1)}.\n \\tag{CE}\\label{eq:CE}$$ In particular, an arbitrarily short fixed final gap may be taken free, with a regularly split incoming state, when classifying terminal shapes. After realizing these data with arbitrarily small exterior errors, every regularity splitting preserving the terminal functional has limiting dominant regularity and summed energy described by $$\\kappa_a=\\kappa s^{p_0a+o(1)},\\qquad E_a=e s^{-da+o(1)}.\n \\tag{CE}\\label{eq:CE}$$ In particular, an arbitrarily short fixed final gap may be taken free, with a regularly split incoming state, when classifying terminal shapes. Equation <a href=\"#eq:CE\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:CE\">[eq:CE]</a> denotes identities of exponent data in this outer closure; it does not assert that one inner sequence attains the closure extrema exactly.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-rt-laws",
        "exact_quote": "For any fixed finite rational list of cuts and names, one can choose the saturated configuration in forward order so that the following properties hold to arbitrarily small exponent errors. At every requested subterminal cut $a$, the selected raw mass and the post-synthesis energy both have size $E_a$. The raw rows have intervalwise regularity at most $s^{-o(1)}\\kappa_a$ and are carried on peeling labels with $$\\label{eq:rt-weight-count}\n \\sum_{\\lambda_a}w_{\\lambda_a}\n       \\le s^{-o(1)}E_a/\\kappa_a.$$ Write $\\mathbf P^a$ for their normalized raw row law. If a portion tested at a later selected cut $l$ can only be reached through a set of relative raw mass $q$ at $i<l$, then its relative mass at $l$ is at most $s^{-o(1)}q^{2/3}$, up to negligible error. <a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Euclidean half-wave propagator** ([source](#sec:introduction)): Let $$\widehat f(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-ix\cdot\xi}f(x)\,dx, \qquad Uf(x,t)=\frac1{(2\pi)^3} \int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{i(x\cdot\xi+t\|\xi\|)}\widehat f(\xi)\,d\xi.$$
- **Bessel potential multiplier** ([source](#sec:introduction)): For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, write $J^\alpha=(1-\Delta)^{\alpha/2}$, with Fourier multiplier $(1+\|\xi\|^2)^{\alpha/2}$.
- **Fixed polynomial setup** ([source](#stmt-def-fw-setup)): A fixed polynomial setup specifies all structural constants, the finite upper bounds on powers of $s^{-1}$ occurring in its hypotheses, and a finite bound on the number of operations along each branch.
- **Relative negligibility** ([source](#stmt-def-fw-setup)): An error $r_s$ is negligible relative to a positive reference quantity $a_s$ if, for every $N>0$, $$\|r_s\|\le C_N s^N a_s$$ for all sufficiently small scales, with $C_N$ independent of scale.
- **Upper growth exponent** ([source](#eq:fw-upper-exponent)): For a nonnegative functional $\mathcal B_s$, define its upper exponent to be $$\label{eq:fw-upper-exponent} \Gamma=\sup_{\mathscr S}\ \sup_{(s_k,\mathcal E_k)} \limsup_{k\to\infty} \frac{\log\mathcal B_{s_k}(\mathcal E_k)}{\log(1/s_k)}.$$
- **Energy** ([source](#pm-h-7)): Energy means a squared Hilbert norm.
- **Conditional surprise score** ([source](#pm-h-10)): For a finite-valued name $X$ and conditioning data $Y$, write $$\label{eq:fw-score} i_s(X\mid Y) =-\frac{\log\mathbb P(X\mid Y)}{\log(1/s)},$$
- **Classical cylinder state** ([source](#stmt-cyl-def-states)): In the *classical cylinder*, $(N,D)$ is another exact index, $D_T=D+TN$, and free evolution leaves the state unchanged in these moving coordinates.
- **Hybrid cylinder state** ([source](#stmt-cyl-def-states)): In the *hybrid cylinder*, $H>0$ is fixed, there is an exact index $\sigma\in[1,2]$, and a fiber state belongs to $L^2(\mathbb R_D;\mathcal H)$.
- **Cylinder tests and regularity** ([source](#stmt-cyl-def-test)): A test $Q$ at $(T,\ell)$ has widths $r>0$, $f\ge d_\ell$, with $f>0$. For a hybrid row observed at the cut $T$, $D_T$ in the following inequalities denotes its instantaneous analyzed center $D$, not an exact classical trajectory. The test is specified by $$\begin{gathered} \|X-x\|\le r,\qquad \|B_T-b\|\le\ell r,\qquad \|Y_T-y-2x(B_T-b)\|\le\ell r^2,\label{cyl:base-test}\\ \|N-c-\alpha X-\beta(T)X^2-K(Y_T-2XB_T)\|\le f, \label{cyl:velocity-test}\\ \|D_T-d-\alpha B_T-\beta(T)Y_T+KB_T^2\|\le\ell f. \label{cyl:position-test} \end{gathered}$$ All centers and coefficients are real. Extend the coefficients by $$\beta(t)=\beta(T)+(t-T)K,\qquad d(t)=d+(t-T)c.$$ The test weight is $w(Q)=r^{3+\eta}f^{1-\eta}$. A row measure is $\kappa$-regular if $\mu(Q)\le\kappa w(Q)$ for every admissible test.
- **Cylinder polynomial setup** ([source](#stmt-cyl-def-setup)): The quantities $e/\kappa,\kappa/e$ and, in the hybrid case, $H,H^{-1}$ are bounded by fixed powers of $s^{-1}$. The initial base support lies in a box of fixed-power size. The initial normal phase has negligible mass relative to $e$ outside such a box. The marginal base density and the joint density in $(X,B,Y,N,D)$ are bounded by $e$ times a fixed power of $s^{-1}$, with respect to Lebesgue measure. Negligibility is uniform within each family to which an exponent bound is applied. All these powers, and the bound on the number of operators on a branch, are fixed before $s\to0$.
- **Documented gate** ([source](#pm-h-15)): A *documented gate* is a row projection followed by synthesis, whose retained rows are partitioned among tests.
- **Curvature displays** ([source](#stmt-names-curvature-displays)): Fix one of the following displays on an entire parameter patch. 1. In the quadratic equality case, write $$b(a)=b_2(a)=c(a-1),\qquad b_1(a)=(c-J)(a-1),\qquad c>0,$$ and put $P^\diamond=P_1(F)$. If $c>1$, let $R_a,k_a$ be the rounded values of $\beta_1(t_a),K_1$, at depths $b(a),b(a)-a$, respectively, and extend $R_a$ with slope $k_a$ from $t_a$. If $c\leq1$, round only $\beta^\diamond=\beta_1(T_1)$ at depth $b(a)$, and set $k_a=0$. 2. In the pure linear case $c_2=0<c_1$, set $R_a=k_a=0$, $b_1(a)=c_1(a-1)$, and take $P^\diamond$ to be the linearized terminal coefficient at the center of its own base test. Earlier tests are replaced by their enclosing linear tests from <a href="#eq:F" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:F">[eq:F]</a>, with vanishing exponent loss. 3. In the strict case $c_2=1$, $q<1$, fix an endpoint $D\in(0,1]$; hybrid applications use $D=1$. Use the encountered label $\lambda_D$, put $P^\diamond=P_D(F)$, and first record $$\bar k=[K_D]_{b_2(D)-D}.$$ Subtract the common shear whose curvature trajectory is $(\bar k t,\bar k)$, with zero other coefficients. All subsequent coordinates in this display are the residual coordinates. Set $$b(a)=b_2(D)+a-D\quad(a\leq D),$$ round the residual $\beta_D(T_D)$ at depth $b(a)$ to obtain $R_a$, and set $k_a=0$. The actual derivative exponent remains $b_1(a)=(q-J)(a-1)$. For $D<1$ the law remains the final classical assigned law; its encountered $D$-label supplies the data. Write $P$ for the specified derivative, after the global subtraction in case (iii).
- **Canonical phase name** ([source](#stmt-names-canonical-name)): The name $\mathcal C(a,v)$ records $\bar k$ when present, $t_a,R_a,k_a$, and $$L=[P-2R_aX+2k_aB_{t_a}]_l.$$ It also records $$[X]_v,\qquad [B_{t_a}]_{a+v},\qquad [Y_{t_a}-2[X]_vB_{t_a}]_{a+2v}.$$ Finally it records the residual normal velocity and position at $t_a$, at depths $w-g,a+w-g$, after subtracting the shear $$\begin{split} N&\longmapsto N-LX-R_aX^2-k_a(Y_{t_a}-2XB_{t_a}),\\ D_{t_a}&\longmapsto D_{t_a}-LB_{t_a}-R_aY_{t_a}+k_aB_{t_a}^2. \end{split}$$ Here $R_a$ in the displayed expressions is its value at $t_a$.
- **Canonical entropy excess** ([source](#stmt-names-canonical-entropy)): On its domain of use, the excess satisfies $$E(a,v)=\mathcal H(a,v)-\mathsf D_0-(p+d)a-W(a,v)\geq0. \tag{canon}\label{eq:canon}$$
- **Admissible side variable** ([source](#stmt-names-side)): Choose one of the following variables $Z$. 1. *Coarse quadratic side.* Suppose $l(a,v)<\min_{[a,D_{\rm end}]}b_1$, and, in the hybrid case, $w(a,v)<0$. Fix $S=\mathcal C(A,V)$ on the same unclipped branch, with $A<a$, $V>v$, and $$V-v\gg(1+c'+\|q\|+J)(a-A)>0.$$ Retain all strict domain inequalities and put $Z=(S,t_a,R_a,k_a)$. When label recovery is needed for $c=1$, also require $v,V<u(a)$ with slack. 2. *Exact quadratic side, classical.* Let $S=(y_0,\bar k,[P^\diamond]_{x_*})$, omitting $\bar k$ when absent, with $x_*>l(a,v)$. The raw coefficient bin must have zero conditional exponent, or arbitrarily small-cost covering lists, given $y_0,t_a$. One may choose $x_*<p_*(a)$, and also $x_*<b_1(D)$ in a virtual comparison. Put $Z=(S,t_a,R_a,k_a)$. 3. *Coarse pure linear side.* Take $S=\mathcal C(A,V)$, with $V-v\gg(1+c')(a-A)>0$, and put $Z=(S,t_a,L)$. Maintain $w<0$ in the hybrid case. 4. *Exact linear side, classical.* Put $Z=(y_0,t_a,\bar k,R_a,k_a,L)$, omitting unused entries. In a clipped branch require $v>b_1-b$, and remain short of a virtual endpoint. The additional bins have zero exponent given $y_0,t_a$, by ownership and <a href="#eq:A" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:A">[eq:A]</a>. The anchors and static coefficient depths are fixed on a patch. Countably many such patches cover all the stated admissible roots.
- **Admissible interior tangent data** ([source](#stmt-int-data)): The common root is $C_*$, the side is $Z$, and the phase $F=F(Z)$ is either $$F=(X,B,P,Y,N,D)\quad\text{in the quadratic case},\qquad F=(X,B,Y,N,D)\quad\text{in the linear case}.$$ Here $D$ denotes the normalized coordinate called $D'_0$ in the tangent construction. Conditional on $Z$, finitely many observations are independent with their prescribed common distribution. Their stored marks are $\Xi_i=(\theta_i,r_i)$, together with $\mathfrak k_i$ in the nonconstant quadratic case. Marks are stored to a sufficiently large finite depth. Set $\mathcal D=(C_*,\boldsymbol\Xi)$. We use the following properties of this construction. 1. The information estimates <a href="#eq:vb" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:vb">[eq:vb]</a> and <a href="#eq:fib" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:fib">[eq:fib]</a> hold for every fixed finite set of phase, angular, and mark queries. In particular the angular score at depth $p$ is $mp+o(1)$. 2. The nested phase and projection names satisfy the score calculus: limiting scores have nonnegative Lipschitz increments; the chain rule, conditioning inequalities, and comparisons by negligible lists hold at actual samples; local mixed-prefix scores are linear at almost every layer. The projection rule stated in the preceding section applies with its specified finite-prefix Frostman hypotheses. 3. The time mark has dimension at least $d$. Given a joint mark parent at depth $p>0$, the joint mark increment on $p\to p+t$ has score at least $dt$, up to strict losses. For $c\geq1$ the time increment itself has this lower bound. For a linear branch with $c>1$, this remains true after conditioning on $r_{p+t}$, provided $p+t<cp$. If $0<c<1$, the mixed mark profile supplies a number $\nu\in[0,1]$ with $$\begin{split} i_\delta(r_{p+t}\mid Z,\theta_{p+t},r_p)&=\nu t+o(t),\\ i_\delta(\theta_{p+t}\mid Z,\theta_p,r_{p+t}) &\geq (d-c\nu)_+t-o(t). \end{split}$$ These assertions are made on the finite queries allowed by that profile; $t$ is chosen small enough relative to $p$. 4. Resampling the side and phase conditionally on $(C_*,\boldsymbol\Xi,Q_i)$ preserves the marked marginal. On a resampling leg, with $A=\Delta X$, the increments obey <a href="#eq:leg" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:leg">[eq:leg]</a> to any fixed tested accuracy. The finite-walk likelihood comparison supplied by <a href="#eq:fib" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:fib">[eq:fib]</a> remains available after conditioning on a common angular prefix when one is used. In the quadratic case, *radial spreading* means that the high alternative of <a href="#eq:rad" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:rad">[eq:rad]</a> has $e_*\geq d$ almost surely for the replicas. For conclusions involving $G_i$ when $c>1$, we also use the stated uniform avoidance of affine lines. In the linear case, *crossing* means that both $\|\theta_i-\theta_j\|$ and $\|r_i-r_j\|$ exceed $\delta^\chi$ with probability tending to one for each fixed $\chi>0$.
- **Contact readings** ([source](#pm-h-48)): On a layer $p\to p+t$, $t\ll p$, use the contact forms $$\label{int:contact} H=dY-2X\,dB,\qquad J=dN-P\,dX,\qquad K=dD-P\,dB$$
- **Round experiment** ([source](#stmt-rt-model)): Write a spacetime point as $(t,b,y)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb R$, and put $$q(t,b,y)=ty-\|b\|^2,\qquad L_A=\partial_t+A\cdot\partial_b+\|A\|^2\partial_y.$$ The classical trajectories are $(B+tA,Y+t\|A\|^2)$, with arbitrary positive phase energy of total mass $e$. The initial phase support has finite-power size, and its density relative to Lebesgue measure is at most $e$ times a finite power of the final scale. These bounds are uniform for the families in a fixed setup. Passive indices, when present, range over standard Borel spaces; separable Hilbert multiplicity is unrestricted. In the wave experiment the initial datum belongs to $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathcal H)$, where $\mathcal H$ is any separable Hilbert space, and has squared norm $e$. Its evolution is $$\widehat{U(t)v}(\xi,-\rho) =e^{-it\|\xi\|^2/(4\rho)}\widehat v(\xi,-\rho).$$ The parameter $H>0$ and its reciprocal have finite-power size, and $H\rho$ belongs to a fixed compact subinterval of $(0,\infty)$. At length $\ell$ set $$d_\ell=(H/\ell)^{1/2},\qquad q_\ell=(H\ell)^{1/2}.$$ The analyzing operator $V_\ell$ applies, for each $A\in\mathbb R^2$, the multiplier $$\chi(H\rho)\psi\bigl((\xi/(2\rho)-A)/d_\ell\bigr), \qquad \int_{\mathbb R^2}\|\psi\|^2=1,$$ and then takes the inverse spatial Fourier transform. Its row measure is $d_\ell^{-2}\,dA\,db\,dy$. Here $\psi$ is smooth and compactly supported, and $\chi$ is smooth, supported in a positive band, and bounded by one. A *plateau analysis* has $\chi=1$ on the incoming spectrum. Such an analysis is isometric; every analysis is contractive. Masks act pointwise by contractions on the rows and are followed by synthesis $V_\ell^*$. After synthesis, subsequent plateau cutoffs may use a fixed band enlargement. Only finitely many cuts at fixed depths are used on any inner sequence. Initial row energy outside a finite-power phase box is smaller than every power of the final scale, relative to $e$.
- **Round regularity** ([source](#stmt-rt-regularity)): A round test imposes $\|x\|,\|z\|,\|V\|\le1$ at $u=0$ and has $f=1$. A hyperquadric test additionally imposes $$\|F\|\le f,\qquad \|G\|\le f,\qquad 0<f\le1,$$ where $$F=c+du+\alpha\cdot x+\beta z+k(uz-\|x\|^2),\qquad G=L_VF,$$ and $$\|\alpha\|^2-4\beta d+4kc=1,\qquad \max(\|c\|,\|d\|,\|\alpha\|,\|\beta\|,\|k\|)\le100.$$ Every test must satisfy $rf\ge d_\ell$. Its weight is $w=r^4f^{1-\eta}$, where $0<\eta<1$ is fixed. Regularity with constant $\kappa$ means $\mu_I(E)\le\kappa w(E)$ for every test $E$. Initial regularity is required, and $e/\kappa$ and $\kappa/e$ have finite-power size. At a final cut one may assign measures dominated in sum by the row energy, with each assignment supported on its own test. Writing their masses as $m_\lambda$, the normalized functional is $$\frac{s^{-1/2}}{e\sqrt\kappa} \sum_\lambda m_\lambda^{3/2}w_\lambda^{-1/2}.$$
- **Round phase name** ([source](#pm-h-73)): Define the phase name $$C(a,v)=\left(T_a,A_v, [b(T_a)]_{\ell_aR_v}, [y(T_a)-2A_v\cdot b(T_a)]_{\ell_aR_v^2}\right). \tag{grid}\label{eq:grid}$$
- **Bochner–Riesz means and maximal operator** ([source](#eq:intro-br-means)): For $R>0$, $\delta>0$, and $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)$, define the Bochner–Riesz means and their maximal operator by $$\label{eq:intro-br-means} \begin{split} B_R^\delta f(x) &=\frac1{(2\pi)^3}\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{ix\cdot\xi} \left(1-\frac{\|\xi\|^2}{R^2}\right)_+^\delta \widehat f(\xi)\,d\xi,\\ B_*^\delta f(x)&=\sup_{R>0}\|B_R^\delta f(x)\|. \end{split}$$
- **Finite-time maximal half-wave** ([source](#sec:introduction)): Define the finite-time maximal half-wave by $U_*f(x)=\sup_{0<t<1}\|Uf(x,t)\|$.
- **Bochner–Riesz critical index** ([source](#stmt-cor-br-nonmaximal)): For $1\le p\le\infty$, with $1/\infty=0$, set $$\delta_{\mathrm{BR}}(p) =\max\left\{3\left\|\frac1p-\frac12\right\|-\frac12,0\right\}.$$

The marginal base density and the joint density in $(X,B,Y,N,D)$ are bounded by $e$ times a fixed power of $s^{-1}$, with respect to Lebesgue measure. Negligibility is uniform within each family to which an exponent bound is applied. All these powers, and the bound on the number of operators on a branch, are fixed before $s\\to0$.",

      "name": "Cylinder polynomial setup",
      "scope": "paper-wide"

          "anchor": "stmt-int-data",
          "exact_quote": "The common root is $C_*$, the side is $Z$, and the phase $F=F(Z)$ is either $$F=(X,B,P,Y,N,D)\\quad\\text{in the quadratic case},\\qquad\n F=(X,B,Y,N,D)\\quad\\text{in the linear case}.$$ Here $D$ denotes the normalized coordinate called $D'_0$ in the tangent construction. Conditional on $Z$, finitely many observations are independent with their prescribed common distribution. Their stored marks are $\\Xi_i=(\\theta_i,r_i)$, together with $\\mathfrak k_i$ in the nonconstant quadratic case. Marks are stored to a sufficiently large finite depth. Set $\\mathcal D=(C_*,\\boldsymbol\\Xi)$.\n\nWe use the following properties of this construction.\n\n1.  The information estimates <a href=\"#eq:vb\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:vb\">[eq:vb]</a> and <a href=\"#eq:fib\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:fib\">[eq:fib]</a> hold for every fixed finite set of phase, angular, and mark queries. In particular the angular score at depth $p$ is $mp+o(1)$.\n\n2.  The nested phase and projection names satisfy the score calculus: limiting scores have nonnegative Lipschitz increments; the chain rule, conditioning inequalities, and comparisons by negligible lists hold at actual samples; local mixed-prefix scores are linear at almost every layer. The projection rule stated in the preceding section applies with its specified finite-prefix Frostman hypotheses.\n\n3.  The time mark has dimension at least $d$. Given a joint mark parent at depth $p>0$, the joint mark increment on $p\\to p+t$ has score at least $dt$, up to strict losses. For $c\\geq1$ the time increment itself has this lower bound. For a linear branch with $c>1$, this remains true after conditioning on $r_{p+t}$, provided $p+t<cp$. If $0<c<1$, the mixed mark profile supplies a number $\\nu\\in[0,1]$ with $$\\begin{split}\n     i_\\delta(r_{p+t}\\mid Z,\\theta_{p+t},r_p)&=\\nu t+o(t),\\\\\n     i_\\delta(\\theta_{p+t}\\mid Z,\\theta_p,r_{p+t})\n       &\\geq (d-c\\nu)_+t-o(t).\n     \\end{split}$$ These assertions are made on the finite queries allowed by that profile; $t$ is chosen small enough relative to $p$.\n\n4.  Resampling the side and phase conditionally on $(C_*,\\boldsymbol\\Xi,Q_i)$ preserves the marked marginal.         {
          "anchor": "stmt-rt-model",
          "exact_quote": "Write a spacetime point as $(t,b,y)\\in\\mathbb R\\times\\mathbb R^2\\times\\mathbb R$, and put $$q(t,b,y)=ty-|b|^2,\\qquad\n L_A=\\partial_t+A\\cdot\\partial_b+|A|^2\\partial_y.$$ The classical trajectories are $(B+tA,Y+t|A|^2)$, with arbitrary positive phase energy of total mass $e$. The initial phase support has finite-power size, and its density relative to Lebesgue measure is at most $e$ times a finite power of the final scale. These bounds are uniform for the families in a fixed setup. Passive indices, when present, range over standard Borel spaces; separable Hilbert multiplicity is unrestricted. In the wave experiment the initial datum belongs to $L^2(\\mathbb R^3;\\mathcal H)$, where $\\mathcal H$ is any separable Hilbert space, and has squared norm $e$. Its evolution is $$\\widehat{U(t)v}(\\xi,-\\rho)\n =e^{-it|\\xi|^2/(4\\rho)}\\widehat v(\\xi,-\\rho).$$ The parameter $H>0$ and its reciprocal have finite-power size, and $H\\rho$ belongs to a fixed compact subinterval of $(0,\\infty)$. At length $\\ell$ set $$d_\\ell=(H/\\ell)^{1/2},\\qquad q_\\ell=(H\\ell)^{1/2}.$$ The analyzing operator $V_\\ell$ applies, for each $A\\in\\mathbb R^2$, the multiplier $$\\chi(H\\rho)\\psi\\bigl((\\xi/(2\\rho)-A)/d_\\ell\\bigr),\n \\qquad \\int_{\\mathbb R^2}|\\psi|^2=1,$$ and then takes the inverse spatial Fourier transform. Its row measure is $d_\\ell^{-2}\\,dA\\,db\\,dy$. Here $\\psi$ is smooth and compactly supported, and $\\chi$ is smooth, supported in a positive band, and bounded by one. A *plateau analysis* has $\\chi=1$ on the incoming spectrum. Such an analysis is isometric; every analysis is contractive. Masks act pointwise by contractions on the rows and are followed by synthesis $V_\\ell^*$. After synthesis, subsequent plateau cutoffs may use a fixed band enlargement. Only finitely many cuts at fixed depths are used on any inner sequence. Initial row energy outside a finite-power phase box is smaller than every power of the final scale, relative to $e$.",

      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-rt-regularity",
          "exact_quote": "A round test imposes $|x|,|z|,|V|\\le1$ at $u=0$ and has $f=1$. A hyperquadric test additionally imposes $$|F|\\le f,\\qquad |G|\\le f,\\qquad 0<f\\le1,$$ where $$F=c+du+\\alpha\\cdot x+\\beta z+k(uz-|x|^2),\\qquad G=L_VF,$$ and $$|\\alpha|^2-4\\beta d+4kc=1,\\qquad\n \\max(|c|,|d|,|\\alpha|,|\\beta|,|k|)\\le100.$$ Every test must satisfy $rf\\ge d_\\ell$. Its weight is $w=r^4f^{1-\\eta}$, where $0<\\eta<1$ is fixed. Regularity with constant $\\kappa$ means $\\mu_I(E)\\le\\kappa w(E)$ for every test $E$. Initial regularity is required, and $e/\\kappa$ and $\\kappa/e$ have finite-power size. At a final cut one may assign measures dominated in sum by the row energy, with each assignment supported on its own test.           "source_id": "PM-079.1"
        }

      "exact_definition": "A round test imposes $|x|,|z|,|V|\\le1$ at $u=0$ and has $f=1$. Its weight is $w=r^4f^{1-\\eta}$, where $0<\\eta<1$ is fixed. Regularity with constant $\\kappa$ means $\\mu_I(E)\\le\\kappa w(E)$ for every test $E$. Initial regularity is required, and $e/\\kappa$ and $\\kappa/e$ have finite-power size. At a final cut one may assign measures dominated in sum by the row energy, with each assignment supported on its own test.
